title: Where to get GeoPDF and GeoTIFF maps
description: Where to download georeferenced GeoPDF and GeoTIFF maps and find XYZ and WMS map services, by country, province and state, free and paid.
intro: TopoKit opens georeferenced GeoPDF and GeoTIFF files, but finding maps for a particular area isn't always easy. I've put together a list of places to get them across Canada, the United States, Australia, New Zealand, the UK and Ireland. It includes free and paid downloads, along with XYZ and WMS map services that you can add to TopoKit and save for offline use.

Each country starts with national map sources, followed by maps for individual provinces, states and regions. Each entry explains what's available, where to get it and whether it's free. I checked the sources in October 2026. For help adding them to TopoKit, see [Raster overlays](https://topokit.ca/manual/raster-overlays/) for files or [Tile layers](https://topokit.ca/manual/tile-layers/) for map services.
Some services need an API key or limit offline downloads, so check each source's terms.

contribute.heading: Add or fix a map
contribute.text: Send a map that belongs here, ask about an area with nothing listed, or report a broken link or a wrong detail. Each link opens an email with a few lines to fill in.

countries.name: Canada
countries.note: Many commercial publishers sell their digital maps only inside an app rather than as files, among them Backroad Mapbooks (its PDF mapbooks are not georeferenced), Clark Geomatics, ITMB and Xavier Maps. Gem Trek, John Baldwin, Trail Ventures BC, Wild Coast and Chrismar sell paper maps.

countries.name: United States
countries.note: Many of the large trail-map publishers sell digital maps only through Avenza or partner apps, among them Tom Harrison, National Geographic Trails Illustrated (its free PDF Quads are not georeferenced), Green Trails, Beartooth, Latitude 40°, Benchmark, Adventure Maps and Purple Lizard. MyTopo prints custom maps but does not sell files.

countries.name: Australia
countries.note: Western Australia sells its topographic sheets as locked, print-only PDFs, and South Australia's Mapland maps were sold through Avenza. Hema, Spatial Vision and ExplorOz sell digital maps inside their own apps.

countries.name: New Zealand
countries.note: The Topo50 and Topo250 series above are free. Paid digital maps in New Zealand are mostly sold inside apps, so there is no paid file to list.

countries.name: United Kingdom
countries.note: Ordnance Survey does not sell the Explorer or Landranger maps to walkers as files: it licenses the 1:25,000 and 1:50,000 rasters to businesses, and sells them to walkers inside apps such as OS Maps, Anquet, Memory-Map and TwoNav. Harvey Maps also sells its digital maps through apps. The free OS files and the hillshade above are the options for TopoKit.

countries.name: Ireland
countries.note: Tailte Éireann (formerly Ordnance Survey Ireland) sells the Discovery 1:50,000 series on paper; its digital mapping is licensed to public bodies through MapGenie, and there is no open raster of it.

sources.name: BC 1:20,000 topographic maps

licence.name: Personal use only
licence.note: the licence in the download forbids commercial use and redistribution

sources.what: The provincial 1:20,000 topographic map, one sheet per BCGS mapsheet, with contours, roads, water and names over shaded relief; the PDF is about 5 MB, the GeoTIFF zip about 10 MB.
steps: Find the mapsheet number with the [BC mapsheet search](https://a100.gov.bc.ca/ext/mtec/public/products/mapsheet): zoom in until the 1:20,000 grid appears and read the number, such as `092B043`.

PDF: open [pub.data.gov.bc.ca/datasets/177864/pdf/](https://pub.data.gov.bc.ca/datasets/177864/pdf/), then the folder named by the first four characters in lower case (`092b`), then the file (`092B043.pdf`).

GeoTIFF: open […/datasets/177864/tif/](https://pub.data.gov.bc.ca/datasets/177864/tif/), then the folder for the UTM zone (`utm07` to `utm11`, or `bcalb` for BC Albers), then the same four-character folder, and download the zip. The `.tif` inside is the map.
sources.previewAlt: Part of BC sheet 092B043: brown contours, red dashed trails and a lake over a pale green hillshade

sources.name: Sunshine Coast Trail section maps
sources.coverage: Sunshine Coast Trail, Powell River, British Columbia
sources.what: Eleven section maps of the 180 km trail at 1:15,000 to 1:35,000, with huts, campsites and kilometre markers; the page does not say so, but the PDFs are georeferenced.
steps: Open the [maps page](https://sunshinecoasttrail.com/plan-your-hike/maps/) and tap a section to open its PDF, then save it.
sources.previewAlt: Part of Sunshine Coast Trail section 7: the trail in yellow over shaded relief, with Confederation Lake and its hut

sources.name: Toporama, the national topographic map
sources.what: Natural Resources Canada's topographic map of the whole country, with contours, waterways, roads, vegetation and place names.
steps: WMS address: `https://maps.geogratis.gc.ca/wms/toporama_en`. The layer is **WMS-Toporama**.
sources.previewAlt: Toporama around Garibaldi Lake: labelled contours in brown, the lake in blue, glacier edges and creek names

sources.name: Scanned NTS paper maps, 1:50,000 and 1:250,000
sources.what: Every printed NTS sheet at 1:50,000 and 1:250,000, scanned and georeferenced, from 1944 to 2005, plus the newer CanTopo sheets for about 2,200 northern areas; no longer updated.
steps: Download the sheet index, [topographic_index_50k.kmz](https://download-telecharger.services.geo.ca/pub/nrcan_rncan/raster/topographic/index/topographic_index_50k.kmz), and read the sheet number over your area, such as `092B05`.

Open the folder for that sheet under […/raster/topographic/50k/](https://download-telecharger.services.geo.ca/pub/nrcan_rncan/raster/topographic/50k/): the first three characters, then the letter, then the two digits (`50k/092/b/05/`).
Download the `canmatrix_geotiff.zip` with the highest edition number (about 10 MB), or the `cantopo_geopdf.zip` when there is one. The 1:250,000 sheets are under `250k/092/b/`.

sources.name: BC Geographic Warehouse WMS
sources.what: A WMS with hundreds of BC government map layers, including contours, trails, forest roads, parks, waterways and avalanche terrain.
steps: Add the WMS address below and pick the layers you want; layer names start with `pub:`.
To see every layer, open the GetCapabilities list.
sources.notes: Useful layers include `pub:WHSE_BASEMAPPING.TRIM_CONTOUR_LINES`, `pub:WHSE_TANTALIS.TA_PARK_ECORES_PA_SVW` (parks), `pub:WHSE_FOREST_TENURE.FTEN_RECREATION_LINES_SVW` (recreation trails) and `pub:WHSE_FOREST_TENURE.FTEN_ROAD_SECTION_LINES_SVW` (forest roads). Each layer keeps its own licence, Open Government Licence or Access Only, shown on its record in the BC Data Catalogue.
sources.previewAlt: Contours, a park, a recreation trail and forest roads near Powell Lake

sources.name: Québec 1:20,000 topographic maps
sources.publisher: Ministère des Ressources naturelles et des Forêts
sources.what: The BDTQ 1:20,000 series, 2,765 sheets covering Québec south of the 52nd parallel, with relief shading; archived, from photography of 1950 to 2006.
steps: As files, open the dataset record and follow **Répertoire complet (format GeoTIFF, projection MTM)**, or use **Télécharger par feuillet** to pick one sheet.
sources.previewAlt: BDTQ 1:20,000 around Mont-Tremblant: green forest, contours, the lake and village roads

sources.name: Ontario topographic base map
sources.what: The provincial topographic base map as a tile service, in muted colours; the cache was last refreshed in 2020.
sources.previewAlt: The Ontario topographic cache in Algonquin: muted green with contours, lakes and creek names

sources.name: US Topo quadrangles
sources.what: The current 7.5-minute, 1:24,000 maps of the whole country, about 65,000 sheets; GeoPDFs of 15 to 45 MB from the USGS, and GeoTIFFs of 3 to 10 MB from topoView.
steps: In [topoView](https://ngmdb.usgs.gov/topoview/viewer/), choose **UST** and **24K**, search a place or tap the map, open the newest record and download the **GeoTIFF** or the **GeoPDF**.
The [USGS Store Map Locator](https://store.usgs.gov/map-locator) has the same GeoPDFs: drop a marker, tap **View Products**, then **View PDF**.
sources.previewAlt: USGS Topo of the Nisqually glaciers on Mount Rainier: contours over hillshade with glacier and creek names

sources.name: Historical USGS topographic maps, 1884 to 2006
sources.what: Every USGS topographic map printed before US Topo, more than 178,000 sheets at 1:24,000 to 1:250,000, as GeoTIFF; older sheets use NAD27.
steps: In topoView, choose **HTMC** and a scale, search or tap the map, use the year slider to narrow the list, and download the **GeoTIFF**.

sources.name: USGS National Map tile services
sources.what: Four live services for the whole country: USGS Topo with contours and shaded relief, Imagery Topo, Imagery Only and Shaded Relief, with detail to about zoom 16.
sources.previewAlt: USGS Imagery Topo of Mount Rainier: contours and names over aerial photography

sources.name: FSTopo, the Forest Service topographic maps
sources.what: The Forest Service 1:24,000 quadrangles for National Forest land, with the agency's roads, trails and boundaries, updated annually.
steps: Open the **FSTopo** page of [Forest Service Digital Maps](https://experience.arcgis.com/experience/9ab8d03e2bec4d7fbfc27ba836e70aed/page/FSTopo), zoom to your area, tap a quad outline and tap **Download PDF** or **Download GeoTiff**. The list below the map can be filtered by state.
The GeoTIFF zip holds two copies of the map, one in UTM and one in geographic coordinates; either one works.

sources.name: Motor Vehicle Use Maps
sources.what: Each National Forest's legal map of the roads and trails open to motor vehicles and when; black and white, no terrain.
steps: On the forest's website: **Visit**, **Maps & Guides**, **Motor Vehicle Use Maps**, then the PDF.

Or in the Forest Service [Map Finder](https://www.fs.usda.gov/media/241668): set **Map Type** to MVUM, find the forest, tap a map outline and download the geospatial PDF. The Avenza links are for Avenza only.

sources.name: BLM georeferenced PDF maps
sources.what: Recreation, travel-management and surface-management maps for BLM land in the western states; coverage and age vary by state, and some states link only to Avenza.
steps: Open the [collection page](https://www.blm.gov/maps/georeferenced-PDFs), pick the state, tap a map title, then the PDF link on its page.

sources.name: NOAA Custom Chart, nautical charts for any area
sources.what: A paper-style nautical chart of any area you draw, at the scale you choose, built from the current electronic chart data; the PDF is georeferenced.
steps: In the [NOAA Custom Chart](https://devgis.charttools.noaa.gov/pod/) app, set a name, scale and page size under **Chart Settings**, tap **Create New Chart** and tap the map to place it.
Under **Export Functions**, select the chart, tap **Export Selected Charts** and save the PDF. The chart is page 1.
sources.previewAlt: NOAA chart symbology in Puget Sound: soundings, a traffic lane and the shoreline at Port Madison

sources.name: AUSTopo and NATMAP 1:250,000 map sheets
sources.what: The national 1:250,000 series, 516 sheets with 50 m contours; AUSTopo is the current series from 2023, updated annually, and the older NATMAP sheets are on the same page.
steps: Open the [1:250,000 map index](https://geoscience-au.maps.arcgis.com/apps/dashboards/7820589ed6954758a9b23a9d596b76a5), tap the sheet outline and follow the download prompt; or search the sheet name in the [GA catalogue](https://ecat.ga.gov.au/geonetwork/) and tap **Download Map (GeoPDF)**.
sources.previewAlt: The Windorah AUSTopo 1:250,000 sheet seen whole: channel country in blue with the red road network

sources.name: Geoscience Australia topographic tile services
sources.what: Two live national services: the Topographic Base Map in the 1:250,000 specification, which stops at zoom 12, and the scanned NATMAP 250K paper series as one seamless map.
sources.previewAlt: The scanned NATMAP 250K sheet around Katoomba in the Blue Mountains, in the printed map's colours

sources.name: New South Wales topographic maps

licence.name: CC BY 4.0
licence.note: for the sheets; the tile service's record says Creative Commons without naming a version

sources.what: The state series at 1:25,000 in the east, 1:50,000 in the centre and 1:100,000 in the west, generated from current data, as GeoPDF sheets and as a seamless tile service.
steps: Sheets: in the [NSW Topographic Map viewer](https://portal.spatial.nsw.gov.au/portal/apps/webappviewer/index.html?id=06e3c2e0de1e4efda863854048c613c6), search a place or tap the map, select the sheet, open the details panel, find the year and tap **more info** to open the file. The sheets are full A1 maps.
Tile service address: `https://maps.six.nsw.gov.au/arcgis/rest/services/public/NSW_Topo_Map/MapServer/tile/{z}/{y}/{x}`
sources.previewAlt: The NSW 1:25,000 topographic map at Katoomba: yellow built-up area, green national park and the railway

sources.name: Queensland topographic base map
sources.what: The state topographic base map as a tile service, with shaded relief, refreshed every May and November.
steps: The QTopo site also prints map sheets as PDF, but does not say they are georeferenced.
sources.previewAlt: The Queensland topographic base map in Lamington National Park: contours over soft relief with walking tracks in purple

sources.name: Tasmania: theLIST base maps

licence.name: CC BY 3.0 AU
licence.note: for the topographic base map, commercial use allowed; Tasmap 1:25,000 is CC BY-NC-ND 3.0 AU, personal use only

sources.what: Two state services: the Topographic base map drawn from current vector data, and Tasmap 25K, the printed 1:25,000 series stitched into one map.
sources.previewAlt: The Tasmap 1:25,000 series at Cradle Valley, with the Overland Track in red

sources.name: LINZ Basemaps: Topo50 and aerial imagery
sources.publisher: Toitū Te Whenua Land Information New Zealand
sources.what: The Topo50 and Topo250 series as one seamless map, plus the national aerial imagery, with a free key that lasts 90 days.
steps: Open [basemaps.linz.govt.nz](https://basemaps.linz.govt.nz/), tap the menu in the top right, choose **Topo Gridless Maps** or **Aerial Imagery** under **Layers**, and under **Individual API keys** tap the copy button beside **XYZ**. The address carries your key: `https://basemaps.linz.govt.nz/v1/tiles/topo-raster/WebMercatorQuad/{z}/{x}/{y}.webp?api=…`
A key lasts 90 days; copy a new one when the tiles stop. If `.webp` tiles do not draw, change the extension to `.png`.
sources.previewAlt: Topo50 above Queenstown: orange roads, contours, the Tiki Trail and the Skyline gondola

sources.name: Topo50 and Topo250 map sheets
sources.publisher: Toitū Te Whenua Land Information New Zealand
sources.what: The 451 Topo50 sheets at 1:50,000 and the 31 Topo250 sheets as GeoTIFFs of the map area without the legend; around 100 MB each.
steps: Find the sheet code on the [Topo50 sheet index](https://www.linz.govt.nz/products-services/maps/new-zealand-topographic-maps/topo50-map-chooser/topo50-sheet-index), open the sheet in the [map chooser](https://www.linz.govt.nz/products-services/maps/new-zealand-topographic-maps/topo50-map-chooser), and tap the **GeoTIFF** link marked **Map area only**. The **TIFF** with the legend is not georeferenced.
The [Topo250 chooser](https://www.linz.govt.nz/products-services/maps/new-zealand-topographic-maps/topo250-map-chooser) works the same way.

sources.name: Topo50 cropped to your area
sources.what: The Topo50 maps on the LINZ Data Service, where a free account lets you crop a rectangle and export only that part as GeoTIFF.
steps: Sign in at [data.linz.govt.nz](https://data.linz.govt.nz/), open the **NZ Topo50 Maps** layer, tap **Crop** and drag a rectangle, then **Export**, **GeoTIFF**, **Create Export**. The download is a zip.

sources.name: TASMAP digital maps
sources.what: The state map series as plain files: each 1:50,000 sheet comes as GeoTIFF, GeoPDF and KMZ, and the archived 1:25,000 and the 1:250,000 sheets cost less.
steps: In the [TASMAP shop](https://tasmapshop.au/), find the sheet, set **Format** to **Digital** and check out. Whole-state bundles: 1:100,000 for A$59.95, 1:25,000 for A$275, 1:50,000 for A$350.

sources.name: Vicmap Topographic Maps

licence.name: Terms not stated on the product pages

sources.what: Victoria's topographic map series as GeoPDFs: more than 10,000 sheets at 1:25,000, 1:50,000 and 1:100,000, plus custom maps.
steps: In [Vicmap Topographic Maps Online](https://vicmaptopo.land.vic.gov.au/), find the map, add it to the cart and pay. A0 sheets run 1 to 40 MB.

sources.name: Meridian Maps digital maps
sources.what: Thirteen four-wheel-drive, touring and walking maps, mostly Victorian, sold as GeoTIFF downloads.
steps: On the map's page, choose **GeoTiff** in the format selector and check out. A five-map Victorian 4WD pack is A$89.75.

sources.name: Maps by Jeff
sources.price: $25 to $30 per map, paper and files together
sources.coverage: Ontario: Algonquin, Killarney, Temagami, French River, Kawartha Highlands, Massasauga
sources.what: The Ontario canoe-country maps (Algonquin, Temagami, Killarney, French River, Kawartha Highlands, the Massasauga); every paper map comes with its digital files by email, a GeoTIFF among them.
steps: Buy the map on [mapsbyjeff.com](https://mapsbyjeff.com); the files arrive by email. There is no digital-only purchase.

sources.name: outrageGIS Great Smoky Mountains GeoPDF pack
sources.what: Two 1:50,000 GeoPDFs of the park with 100 ft contours, a UTM grid and the backcountry campsites, plus GPX files, as one 250 MB download.
steps: Buy the pack, download it and unzip it. The same maps are on Avenza; this is the copy you own.

sources.name: OS Maps API, the Outdoor style

licence.name: OS OpenData, Open Government Licence
licence.note: for the open zoom levels; the API terms on caching could not be read, so check them before a large offline download

sources.what: Ordnance Survey's own map tiles. The Outdoor, Road and Light styles are free from zoom 7 to 16 with a free key.
steps: Create a free account at [osdatahub.os.uk](https://osdatahub.os.uk/) on the OS OpenData plan, open **API Projects**, make a project and add **OS Maps API**; the project page shows the key.

Address: `https://api.os.uk/maps/raster/v1/zxy/Outdoor_3857/{z}/{x}/{y}.png?key=YOURKEY`. Zoom 17 and beyond is premium and charged. The API terms on caching could not be read; check them before a large offline download.
sources.notes: The Leisure style, which looks like the Explorer maps, is published only in British National Grid tiling, which TopoKit cannot stream.

sources.name: OS OpenData raster maps: VectorMap District, OpenMap Local, 1:250,000
sources.what: Ordnance Survey's free maps of Great Britain as GeoTIFF: VectorMap District, OpenMap Local and the 1:250,000 road map. None has the contours and footpaths of an Explorer map.
steps: Open the download page for the product, choose **GeoTIFF** and, for VectorMap District and OpenMap Local, the 100 km grid square (NN for Fort William, NY for the Lakes, SH for Snowdonia, TQ for London). A square is 100 to 1,100 MB and unzips to many tiles in British National Grid.
sources.notes: VectorMap District comes in 10 km tiles, OpenMap Local in 5 km tiles, and the 1:250,000 map as one 134 MB zip.

sources.name: Environment Agency LiDAR hillshade
sources.what: A hillshade rendered from the 1 m LiDAR terrain model covering almost all of England, served live.
steps: WMS address: `https://environment.data.gov.uk/spatialdata/lidar-composite-digital-terrain-model-dtm-1m/wms`. The layer is **Lidar_Composite_Hillshade_DTM_1m**.
The surface model with trees and buildings is the same address with `digital-surface-model-last-return-dsm-1m` in place of `digital-terrain-model-dtm-1m`.
sources.previewAlt: The Environment Agency 1 m hillshade of Wasdale: Scafell's ridges and the valley floor in grey relief

sources.name: Historic Ordnance Survey maps

licence.name: CC BY 3.0 with conditions
licence.note: personal use on the free MapTiler plan; the one-inch Seventh Series and 1:25,000 Provisional layers are restricted to non-commercial use

sources.what: The library's georeferenced scans of the old OS series as tile layers, served through MapTiler with a free key that allows 100,000 tiles a month.
steps: Create a free account at [cloud.maptiler.com](https://cloud.maptiler.com/) and copy the key.

Address: `https://api.maptiler.com/tiles/uk-osgb63k1955/{z}/{x}/{y}.jpg?key=YOURKEY` for the one-inch Seventh Series; `uk-osgb10k1888` is the six-inch maps, `uk-osgb25k1937` the 1:25,000 Provisional edition.

sources.name: OSNI open data rasters
sources.what: Northern Ireland's open base mapping as georeferenced rasters: the 1:10,000 Mid Scale Raster of the whole province and the StreetMaps of its towns, without contours.
steps: Open the [Mid Scale Raster record](https://www.data.gov.uk/dataset/48376012-8061-4369-8cf5-24961f2f02c6/osni-open-data-1-10-000-raster-mid-scale-raster) and download the zip. The files are in Irish Grid.

sources.name: BGS geology at 1:50,000
sources.what: Bedrock and superficial geology for all of Great Britain, drawn live between 1:100,000 and 1:25,000.
steps: WMS address: `https://map.bgs.ac.uk/arcgis/services/BGS_Detailed_Geology/MapServer/WMSServer`. Layers: **BGS.50k.Bedrock**, **BGS.50k.Superficial.deposits**.
sources.previewAlt: BGS 1:50,000 bedrock geology around Wasdale: the Borrowdale volcanics and the Eskdale granite in colour

sources.name: OSNI 1:50,000 and 1:25,000 raster maps
sources.price: £35.50 per 20 km 1:50,000 tile, £86.20 per 1:25,000 Activity Map, before VAT

licence.name: Terms not stated on the product pages

sources.what: The Discoverer-series 1:50,000 maps and the six 1:25,000 Activity Maps as TIFF files from the government map shop; priced for business use, but files you own.
steps: Pick the tile or map in the shop, choose the TIF format, pay and download.

sources.name: Minnesota DNR Mobile Maps
sources.what: More than 800 Minnesota DNR recreation maps as GeoPDFs: state parks, state forests, trails, OHV areas, hunter walking trails, trout streams and water trails.
steps: Open Mobile Maps and agree to the terms.
Filter by map topic or name, or click the map to list the maps that cover that spot.
Click Download beside the map; the GeoPDF opens in a new tab, where you save it.
sources.notes: 99 state parks, 34 state forests, 40 state trails, 85 OHV areas and 305 hunter walking trails. Files are named <map> GEO.pdf.

sources.name: BC hunting management unit maps
sources.what: Hunting management unit maps for all eight BC regions as GeoPDFs, plus maps of closed areas and special seasons, about two-thirds of them georeferenced.
steps: Open the Hunting and Trapping Regulations Synopsis page.
Under Management unit maps, download the map for your region.
For closed areas and special seasons, expand your region under Detailed Hunting and Trapping Synopsis maps.
sources.notes: The region maps are 26 to 48 MB. The area maps that are not georeferenced are mostly the small Peace region closure maps and the Vancouver Island highway maps.

sources.name: BC motor vehicle prohibition maps
sources.what: Close to 200 georeferenced PDF maps of the areas where motor vehicles, ATVs, e-bikes or snowmobiles are prohibited or restricted, on one page per hunting region.
steps: Open the Motor Vehicle Prohibitions page and choose your region under Motor vehicle prohibition and restriction maps.
Download the map for the area.
sources.notes: The province says more maps will move to these pages; until then the rest are in the hunting synopsis.

sources.name: BC snowmobile closure maps
sources.what: Georeferenced PDF maps of the snowmobile closures in the mountain caribou range, with open riding areas and trails, as regional overviews and detailed sheets.
steps: Open the Snowmobile Closures page.
Download the regional overview or the detailed sheet for the area.
sources.notes: The same closures are on the page as KML and GPX.

sources.name: BC imagery and hillshade WMS
sources.what: BC's imagery WMS, with a province-wide hillshade in grey or colour, painted relief, and older air photo and satellite mosaics.
sources.notes: Hillshade layers are `hillshade_bc_bcalb_hillshade_clr_315` (colour) and `hillshade_bc_bcalb_hillshade_bw_315` (grey).
sources.previewAlt: The colour hillshade layer around Squamish

sources.name: Lake Superior Provincial Park route maps
sources.what: Eight canoe route and walk-in route maps of Lake Superior Provincial Park, published as GeoPDFs.
steps: Open the park's Maps page on ontarioparks.ca.
Download a canoe route or walk-in route map; the park map, the campground maps and the Sand River map are plain PDFs.

sources.name: Queen Elizabeth II Wildlands backcountry map
sources.coverage: Queen Elizabeth II Wildlands Provincial Park
sources.what: The park's backcountry hiking and canoe route map, published as a GeoPDF.
steps: Open the park's Maps page on ontarioparks.ca and download the backcountry hiking and canoe routes map.

sources.name: Alaska statewide imagery 2020
sources.publisher: Alaska Geospatial Office (DNR Division of Geological & Geophysical Surveys) / Maxar
sources.coverage: State of Alaska (full extent roughly 180W to 130W, 52N to 72N)
sources.what: 50 cm Maxar satellite mosaic of the whole state from 2020, cached to zoom 23.
sources.notes: A colour-infrared version is served as `ahri_2020_cir_cache` on the same server.
sources.previewAlt: Alaska 2020 imagery near Anchorage

sources.name: Alaska SPOT5 imagery 2013
sources.what: 2.5 m SPOT5 satellite imagery of the state from 2013, cached to zoom 23.
sources.notes: Panchromatic and colour-infrared versions are `spot5_2013_pan_cache` and `spot5_2013_cir_cache` on the same server.

sources.name: ADF&G custom hunt maps
sources.publisher: Alaska Department of Fish and Game
sources.coverage: Alaska, any area the user frames in the map builder (by species, GMU, hunt type or hunt number)
sources.what: Hunt maps you build at hunt.alaska.gov, with game management unit and subunit boundaries, special areas and federal land over a choice of basemap, saved as a georeferenced PDF.
steps: Open hunt.alaska.gov and go to Maps.
Choose Make a custom map, add the overlays you want and zoom to your area.
Select Print and save the PDF.
sources.notes: A higher zoom gives a sharper map; a large hunt may need several.

sources.name: USFWS Alaska refuge land status maps
sources.publisher: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Alaska Region (Region 7) Division of Realty
sources.coverage: National Wildlife Refuges in Alaska (Alaska Maritime NWR 1:250,000 sheets not online)
sources.what: Land ownership maps of Alaska's national wildlife refuges at 1:250,000 and 1:30,000, as GeoPDFs.
steps: Open the land status map series app.
Pick the refuge and sheet from the index and download the GeoPDF.
sources.notes: The 1:250,000 sheets are updated quarterly and the 1:30,000 sheets each January; the 1:30,000 sheets are up to 56 × 62 inches.

sources.name: USFWS Alaska guide use area maps
sources.publisher: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Alaska Region (Region 7) Division of Realty
